questions.question: A car travels x km at 40 km/hr, another x km at 60 km/hr and 2x km at 80 km/hr. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume x is the LCM of 40 and 60, i.e., x = 120 km.

Total distance = 120 + 120 + 2(120) = 480 km.

Total time = (120 ÷ 40) + (120 ÷ 60) + (240 ÷ 80) = 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 hours.

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 480 ÷ 8 = 60 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Speeds are 40 km/hr, 60 km/hr, and 80 km/hr for distances x, x, and 2x respectively.

Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2260db3578569eb20a8c4ae7e5d938bd60056223fe87c99f094678bbebe6e36b.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = x + x + 2x = 4x km

⇒ Time for first part (t₁) = x ÷ 40 hr

⇒ Time for second part (t₂) = x ÷ 60 hr

⇒ Time for third part (t₃) = 2x ÷ 80 = x ÷ 40 hr

⇒ Total Time = (x ÷ 40) + (x ÷ 60) + (x ÷ 40)

⇒ Total Time = (2x ÷ 40) + (x ÷ 60) = (x ÷ 20) + (x ÷ 60)

⇒ Total Time = (3x + x) ÷ 60 = 4x ÷ 60 = x ÷ 15 hr

⇒ Average Speed = 4x ÷ (x ÷ 15) = 4x × (15 ÷ x)

⇒ Average Speed = 4 × 15 = 60 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed is 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a person travels at different speeds for equal time intervals, the average speed is the arithmetic mean: (v₁ + v₂ + ... + vₙ) ÷ n.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of ‘urban local government’ according to the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Municipality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Municipality** is a type of urban local government in India, constitutionalized through the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992**. It is designed to provide a framework for self-governance in urban areas. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• According to **Article 243-Q** of the **Constitution of India**, there are three types of municipalities: **Nagar Panchayats** for transitional areas, **Municipal Councils** for smaller urban areas, and **Municipal Corporations** for larger urban areas.
 
• The **74th Amendment** added a new **Part IX-A** to the Constitution, titled 'The Municipalities', covering **Articles 243-P to 243-ZG**.
 
• This amendment also introduced the **12th Schedule** to the Constitution, which contains a list of **18 functional items** that fall under the jurisdiction of urban local bodies, such as **urban planning**, **public health**, and **fire services**.
 
• The urban local bodies are intended to ensure democratic decentralization and empower citizens living in cities and towns to manage their local affairs efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rural Local Government (Panchayati Raj):**

 
 
• **Zila Panchayat**: This is the third and highest tier of the **Panchayati Raj System**, functioning at the **district level**. It is a rural local government body. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Block Panchayat**: Also known as **Panchayat Samiti**, it serves as the intermediate tier between the village and the district level in the rural governance structure. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Gram Sabha**: It is the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system, consisting of all persons registered in the **electoral rolls** of a village within the area of the **Gram Panchayat**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The rural local bodies were constitutionalized by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which added **Part IX** and the **11th Schedule** (containing **29 functional items**) to the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **History of Urban Governance:**
 
 
• The first **Municipal Corporation** in India was set up in **Madras** in the year **1688**.
 
• Later, Municipal Corporations were established in **Bombay** and **Calcutta** in **1726**.
 
• **Lord Ripon** is known as the '**Father of Local Self-Government**' in India due to his resolution of **1882**, which provided a roadmap for local self-rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Composition and Duration:**

 
 
• All members of a **Municipality** are **directly elected** by the people of the municipal area. For this purpose, the municipal area is divided into territorial constituencies called **wards**.
 
• The **Constitution** provides for a fixed **five-year term** of office for every municipality. However, it can be dissolved before the completion of its term.
 
• In case of dissolution, elections to constitute the new municipality must be completed within **six months** from the date of its dissolution.
 
 
 
• **Reservations:**
 
 
• Seats are reserved for **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** in every municipality in proportion to their population.
 
• The Act also mandates the reservation of **not less than one-third** of the total number of seats for **women** (including the number of seats reserved for SC/ST women).
 
 
 
• **State Election Commission:**
 
 
• The superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of **electoral rolls** and the conduct of all elections to the municipalities are vested in the **State Election Commission**.

questions.question: A trader marked the price of an item 40% above the cost price. He allowed two successive discounts of 20% and 25% to a customer. If he incurred a loss of ₹224, at what price did he sell the item to that customer?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discount of 20% and 25% = 20 + 25 − (20 × 25)/100 = 40%

Let CP = 100. Then MP = 140 (40% mark-up).

SP = 140 − 40% of 140 = 140 − 56 = 84 units.

Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 84 = 16 units.

16 units → ₹224 ⇒ 1 unit → ₹14.

Selling Price = 84 units × 14 = ₹1,176.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,176.**

questions.question:
Find the simplified value of the following expression:

 ((8.4)/(0.7) + (2.4)/(4)) div ((9.6)/(8) - (3)/(5))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve inner terms: (12 + 0.6) ÷ (1.2 − 0.6)

Evaluate brackets: 12.6 ÷ 0.6

Simplify division: 126 ÷ 6 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: (8.4/0.7 + 2.4/4) ÷ (9.6/8 − 3/5)

Method: Apply BODMAS rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ Term 1: 8.4 ÷ 0.7 = 84 ÷ 7 = 12

⇒ Term 2: 2.4 ÷ 4 = 0.6

⇒ Term 3: 9.6 ÷ 8 = 1.2

⇒ Term 4: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6

Substitute back into expression:

⇒ (12 + 0.6) ÷ (1.2 − 0.6)

⇒ 12.6 ÷ 0.6

⇒ 126 ÷ 6 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: Brackets (), Of/Orders, Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Decimal Division Shortcut

To divide decimals, multiply both numerator and denominator by 10, 100, etc., to make the divisor a whole number (e.g., 8.4/0.7 = 84/7).

Fraction to Decimal Conversion

Converting common fractions like 3/5 to 0.6 or 1/4 to 0.25 often simplifies complex multi-step expressions.

questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 38%. If the cost price is increased by ₹68 and the selling price is reduced by ₹54, then the profit would be 37.5%. What is the original cost price (in ₹) of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio CP : SP = 100 : 138 = 50 : 69

Final Ratio CP : SP (at 37.5% profit) = 8 : 11

Using Cross-Multiplication: (50 × 11 − 69 × 8) units = (8 × −54 − 11 × 68)

|550 − 552| units = |−432 − 748| ⇒ 2 units = 1180

1 unit = 590 ⇒ Original CP (50 units) = 50 × 590 = 29500

**∴ The correct answer is 29500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Profit = 38%

Change in CP = + ₹68

Change in SP = − ₹54

New Profit = 37.5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/812ccfb8ce0cbb909a3bc1351145d1be25ad778b36f7060ba538e6ddb117601c.png] 

Let original CP = x

⇒ Original SP = 1.38x

⇒ New CP = x + 68

⇒ New SP = 1.38x − 54

⇒ New Profit = 37.5% = 37.5/100 = 3/8

⇒ New SP = New CP × (1 + 3/8) = New CP × 11/8

⇒ 1.38x − 54 = (x + 68) × 11/8

⇒ 8 × (1.38x − 54) = 11 × (x + 68)

⇒ 11.04x − 432 = 11x + 748

⇒ 11.04x − 11x = 748 + 432

⇒ 0.04x = 1180

⇒ x = 1180 / 0.04 = 118000 / 4

⇒ x = 29500

**∴ The correct answer is 29500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basic Relation

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 or SP = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100.

Marked Price and Discount

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100. Relation between CP and MP: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Successive Percentage Change

Effective change = a + b + (ab/100). This applies to successive discounts and multi-stage price changes.

Dishonest Dealer

Profit % = [Error / (True Value − Error)] × 100, when the dealer uses faulty weights.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exercise Varuna** is a high-profile bilateral **Naval Exercise** conducted annually between the **Indian Navy** and the **French Navy** (Marine Nationale).
 
• The bilateral naval cooperation between **India** and **France** was initiated in the year **1983**. It serves as a vital pillar of the **strategic partnership** between the two nations.
 
• The exercise was officially named **'Varuna'** in **2001**. Since then, it has grown in scope and complexity, evolving into a sophisticated multi-domain maritime operation.
 
• The **2025** edition, like its predecessors, focuses on enhancing **interoperability**, improving **maritime security**, and fostering mutual cooperation in the **Indo-Pacific** region.
 
• The exercise typically includes advanced **anti-submarine warfare (ASW)** maneuvers, tactical firing drills, **visit, board, search, and seizure (VBSS)** operations, and complex maneuvers at sea.
 
• Both countries deploy their frontline naval assets, including **guided-missile frigates**, **tankers**, **maritime patrol aircraft**, and **integral helicopters**, to demonstrate their maritime prowess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Indo-French Exercises**:

 
 
• **Exercise Garuda**: A major bilateral exercise between the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** and the **French Air and Space Force**.
 
• **Exercise Shakti**: A biennial joint military exercise conducted between the **Indian Army** and the **French Army**, focusing on counter-terrorism operations.
 
• **FRINJEX**: A joint military exercise involving the **Indian Army** and the **French Army**, recently introduced to further boost defense ties.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Partnership**: **India** and **France** established a **Strategic Partnership** in **January 1998**. France was the first Western country with which India signed such an agreement, covering **defense**, **civil nuclear energy**, and **space**.
 
• **Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA)**: Both nations collaborate extensively on **Maritime Domain Awareness** in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**. France has a permanent presence in the **Indian Ocean** through its overseas territories like **Reunion Island** and **Mayotte**.
 
• **Defense Acquisitions**: The defense relationship is bolstered by significant procurement programs, such as the **Rafale fighter jets** for the **IAF** and the **Scorpene-class (Kalvari class) submarines** built in **India** at **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL)** with French technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indo-Pacific Stability**: **Exercise Varuna** is crucial for maintaining a **Free, Open, and Inclusive Indo-Pacific**. It acts as a deterrent against maritime threats like **piracy** and **illegal fishing**.
 
• **Technical Interoperability**: The exercise allows both navies to practice **cross-deck landings** and personnel exchanges, which is essential for coordinated action during **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR)** missions.
 
• **Geopolitical Significance**: The continuity of **Varuna** through various global geopolitical shifts highlights the **reliability** and **depth** of the **New Delhi-Paris** axis in the **21st century**.

questions.question: On a certain amount, if at the same rate of interest, the simple interest for 2 years is ₹64 and the compound interest is ₹72, then find that amount (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SI for 1 year = 64 ÷ 2 = ₹32

Difference (Interest on interest) = 72 − 64 = ₹8

Rate (R) = (8 ÷ 32) × 100 = 25%

Principal (P) = (32 × 100) ÷ 25 = ₹128

**∴ The correct answer is ₹128.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹64

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹72

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Rate (R) = (Difference × 100) ÷ (SI for 1 year)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2bb047929ce8e005a1eda332a96c1b7c599e6359d98bb01abd0d187aa0e40088.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ SI for 1 year = 64 ÷ 2 = ₹32

⇒ Interest for 1st year is same for SI and CI = ₹32

⇒ CI for 2nd year = Total CI − 1st year CI = 72 − 32 = ₹40

⇒ Difference (Interest on 1st year interest) = 40 − 32 = ₹8

⇒ Rate of interest (R) = (8 ÷ 32) × 100 = 25%

⇒ Principal (P) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ (R × 1)

⇒ P = (32 × 100) ÷ 25

⇒ P = ₹128

**∴ The correct answer is ₹128.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference (D) is given by D = P × (R/100)².

Direct Rate Formula for 2 years

Rate R = [2 × (CI − SI) ÷ SI] × 100, where SI is for 2 years.

Effective Rate of CI

For 2 years, effective rate = R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.

questions.question: Among five people named V, W, X, Y and Z, each have a certain age. The age of X is 12. V is four times the age of Z. Y is half the age of V. W is thrice the age of X. If Z is one ninth the age of W, what is the age of Y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Start with the known value X = 12.

W = 3 × 12 = 36.

Z = 36 ÷ 9 = 4.

V = 4 × 4 = 16.

Y = 16 ÷ 2 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: X = 12, W = 3X, Z = W/9, V = 4Z, Y = V/2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d070c9f3fb8d88c9be4fee6ca526eadf5196cdd949dd1fa6a9661326cc3501d.png] 

⇒ Age of X = 12

⇒ Age of W = 3 × X = 3 × 12 = 36

⇒ Age of Z = (1/9) × W = 36 ÷ 9 = 4

⇒ Age of V = 4 × Z = 4 × 4 = 16

⇒ Age of Y = (1/2) × V = 16 ÷ 2 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

If A is n times B, then A = n × B. If C is 1/m of D, then C = D ÷ m.

Average Age

The average age of n people is the sum of their ages divided by n.

Constant Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant regardless of the number of years passed.

70, 70, 73, 71, 74, 69, 80, 68, 66, 66, 89, 83, 81, 86, 82, 74, 86, 87, 67, 72, 62, 76, 86, 65, 62

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in a dataset.

Frequency of 86 → 3 times (Max occurrence)

Frequency of 70, 74, 66, 62 → 2 times each

Other values → 1 time each

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Formula: Mode = Value with highest frequency

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18b47449b3517c5d7dacfdff0eac00c2efec14796e9d6f0a6c2863d1fd66a73d.png] 

⇒ Count of 86 = 3

⇒ Count of 70 = 2

⇒ Count of 74 = 2

⇒ Count of 66 = 2

⇒ Count of 62 = 2

⇒ All other numbers = 1

⇒ Highest Frequency = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between the three measures of central tendency is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean

Mean is the average calculated by summing all values and dividing by the total count: Σx ÷ n.

Median

The median is the middle value when the data is arranged in ascending or descending order. If n is even, it is the average of the two middle terms.

questions.question: A force acts on a 4 kg body at rest and produces an acceleration of 3 m/s². The final velocity after 5 seconds is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 m/s**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the **final velocity** of the body, we use the **first equation of motion**: v = u + at, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, **a** is the acceleration, and **t** is the time duration.
 
• According to the question, the body starts from **rest**, which means the **initial velocity (u)** is 0 m/s.
 
• The **acceleration (a)** produced by the force is given as 3 m/s².
 
• The **time interval (t)** for which the force acts is 5 seconds.
 
• Substituting these values into the equation: v = 0 + (3 * 5).
 
• The calculation results in **v = 15 m/s**.
 
• The **mass** of the body (4 kg) is provided in the problem but is not required to calculate the final velocity since the acceleration is already known. If the force were given instead of acceleration, the mass would be used to find acceleration via **Newton's Second Law** (F = ma).
 
• Therefore, options like 10 m/s, 12 m/s, or 20 m/s are incorrect based on the standard kinematic calculation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:** It states that the force acting on an object is equal to the product of its **mass** and **acceleration** (F = ma). In this case, the force acting on the body would be 4 kg * 3 m/s² = 12 **Newtons (N)**.
 
• **Equations of Motion:** These equations are applicable only when the **acceleration** is **constant** (uniform acceleration).
 
• **Acceleration:** It is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to time. Its **SI unit** is m/s².
 
• **Velocity:** It is a **vector quantity** that specifies both the speed and the direction of motion. Its SI unit is **m/s**.

questions.question: Which of the following events happens when lysosomes in a cell burst?

options.text: Enzymes digest the cell’s own components

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enzymes digest the cell’s own components**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are small, membrane-bound sac-like structures found in eukaryotic cells that contain powerful **hydrolytic enzymes**.
 
• These enzymes are capable of breaking down all types of biological polymers such as proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and carbohydrates.
 
• When a cell gets damaged or undergoes cellular metabolism disturbances, the **lysosomal membrane** may rupture or burst.
 
• Once released into the **cytoplasm**, these digestive enzymes begin to break down the cell's own organelles and structural components, leading to the death of the cell.
 
• This process of self-digestion is scientifically referred to as **Autolysis**.
 
• Due to this ability to destroy their own cell, lysosomes are commonly known as the **Suicidal Bags** of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Discovery:** Lysosomes were discovered by the Belgian cytologist **Christian de Duve** in 1955.
 
• **Acidic Environment:** The enzymes inside lysosomes (like proteases, nucleases, and glycosidases) work most efficiently at an **acidic pH** of approximately 4.5 to 5.0.
 
• **Autophagy:** This is a related process where lysosomes digest old or damaged organelles to recycle their components, helping in **cellular renovation**.
 
• **Function:** Apart from autolysis, they are essential for **intracellular digestion** of nutrients and the destruction of foreign invading particles like **bacteria and viruses**.
 
• **Occurrence:** They are predominantly found in **animal cells**; while similar structures exist in plants, they are often referred to as specialized vacuoles.

questions.question:
Consider the following chemical reactions:

I: BaCl₂ (aq) + Na₂SO₄ (aq) → BaSO₄ (s) + 2NaCl (aq)

II: Pb(NO₃)₂ (aq) + KI (aq) → PbI₂ (s) + 2KNO₃(aq)

Which of the following correctly classifies these reactions?

options.text: I: Double displacement reaction; II: Displacement reaction
I: Displacement reaction; II: Double displacement reaction
I: Double displacement reaction; II: Neutralisation reaction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both are double displacement reactions**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Double Displacement Reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where two compounds react, and the **positive ions (cations)** and the **negative ions (anions)** of the two reactants switch places to form two new compounds.
 
• In **Reaction I**: BaCl₂ (aq) + Na₂SO₄ (aq) rightarrow BaSO₄ (s) + 2NaCl (aq) , the **Barium ions** (Ba²⁺) and **Sodium ions** (Na⁺) exchange their partner anions (Chloride and Sulfate). This results in the formation of **Barium sulfate** and **Sodium chloride**.
 
• In **Reaction II**: Pb(NO₃)₂ (aq) + 2KI (aq) rightarrow PbI₂ (s) + 2KNO₃ (aq) , the **Lead ions** (Pb²⁺) and **Potassium ions** (K⁺) exchange their anions (Nitrate and Iodide), forming **Lead iodide** and **Potassium nitrate**.
 
• Both reactions involve the exchange of ions between the reactants, which is the defining characteristic of a **double displacement reaction**.
 
• These are not **displacement reactions** (or single displacement) because in a single displacement, one element replaces another element in a compound. Here, two compounds are mutually exchanging components.
 
• While **neutralization** is a type of double displacement, it specifically involves an **acid** and a **base** reacting to form **water** and a **salt**, which is not the case in these specific reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Double displacement reactions that result in the formation of an insoluble solid are also called **Precipitation Reactions**.
 
• In Reaction I, **Barium sulfate** ( BaSO₄ ) forms a **white precipitate**.
 
• In Reaction II, **Lead iodide** ( PbI₂ ) forms a distinct **yellow precipitate**.
 
• These reactions generally occur in **aqueous solutions** where the ions are free to move and interact.
 
• The general representation of a double displacement reaction is: **AB + CD → AD + CB**.

questions.question: A number is decreased by 18% and then increased by 22%. Find the net increase or decrease percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply successive percentage formula: Net change % = a + b + (ab/100)

Where a = −18 (decrease) and b = +22 (increase).

Net change = −18 + 22 + [(−18 × 22) / 100]

Net change = 4 − (396 / 100) = 4 − 3.96 = +0.04%

Positive result indicates an increase.

**∴ The correct answer is Increased 0.04%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First change = 18% decrease

Second change = 22% increase

**Formula Used:**

Net Percentage Change = [a + b + (a × b / 100)]%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59eb0ee881f5901065055bc959d956ae7cbfdbd5e781821ebb960ff00c104d99.png] 

⇒ Let the initial number be 100 units.

⇒ Step 1: Decrease by 18%.

⇒ Value after decrease = 100 − (18% of 100) = 100 − 18 = 82.

⇒ Step 2: Increase by 22%.

⇒ Value after increase = 82 + (22% of 82)

⇒ 22% of 82 = (22 × 82) / 100 = 1804 / 100 = 18.04.

⇒ Final value = 82 + 18.04 = 100.04.

⇒ Net Change = Final Value − Initial Value = 100.04 − 100 = 0.04.

⇒ Percentage change = (0.04 / 100) × 100 = 0.04%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increased 0.04%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then by y%, the effective change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%. Use positive for increase and negative for decrease.

Multiplying Factor Method

Net value = Initial Value × (1 + x/100) × (1 + y/100). For 18% decrease and 22% increase, multiplier = 0.82 × 1.22 = 1.0004.

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂%, the single equivalent discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁d₂/100)]%.

questions.question: If the median and mode of a data of 20 numbers are 250 and 295, respectively, then find the sum of the 20 numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply Empirical Formula: Mean = (3 × Median − Mode) ÷ 2

Mean = (3 × 250 − 295) ÷ 2 = 455 ÷ 2 = 227.5

Sum of 20 numbers = Mean × Total numbers

Sum = 227.5 × 20 = 4550

**∴ The correct answer is 4550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Median (Md) = 250

Mode (Mₒ) = 295

Total numbers (N) = 20

**Formula Used:**

Empirical relationship: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

Sum of terms = Mean × N

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb7935dab386037219028fa5a7845eb740ae826acb4026217a3cd3c633069b48.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 295 = 3 × 250 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 295 = 750 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 2 × Mean = 750 − 295 ⇒ 2 × Mean = 455 ⇒ Mean = 227.5 ⇒ Sum of 20 numbers = Mean × N ⇒ Sum = 227.5 × 20 ⇒ Sum = 4550

**∴ The correct answer is 4550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Arithmetic Mean

Mean = (Σxᵢ) ÷ N. It is the average of all observations in a data set.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical (normal) distribution, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness

If Mean < Median < Mode, the distribution is negatively skewed. If Mode < Median < Mean, it is positively skewed.

questions.question: When white light passes through a prism, different colours of light bend through different angles. Which colour bends the least and which bends the most?

options.text: Both red and violet bend equally
Red bends the most, violet bends the least
Red bends the least, violet bends the most
Blue bends the least, yellow bends the most

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red bends the least, violet bends the most**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a beam of **white light** passes through a glass prism, it splits into its constituent colors. This phenomenon is known as **Dispersion of Light**.
 
• The band of seven colors obtained is called a **spectrum**, consisting of **Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red (VIBGYOR)**.
 
• The **refractive index** of glass is different for different colors (wavelengths). According to **Cauchy's formula**, the refractive index is inversely proportional to the wavelength.
 
• **Red light** has the **longest wavelength** in the visible spectrum. Because it travels faster through the glass compared to other colors, it is deviated by the **minimum angle** and thus **bends the least**.
 
• **Violet light** has the **shortest wavelength** in the visible spectrum. It travels the slowest through the glass prism, resulting in the **maximum angle of deviation**, meaning it **bends the most**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Isaac Newton** was the first scientist to use a glass prism to obtain the spectrum of sunlight and demonstrate that white light is made of seven colors.
 
• The **Angle of Deviation** is the angle between the direction of the incident ray and the emergent ray. It depends on the **angle of the prism**, the **angle of incidence**, and the **refractive index** of the material.
 
• A **Rainbow** is a natural spectrum appearing in the sky after rain, caused by the **dispersion**, **refraction**, and **internal reflection** of sunlight by tiny water droplets acting as small prisms.
 
• In a vacuum, all colors of light travel at the same speed (approximately 3 times 10⁸ meters per second), but their speeds differ when they enter a **dispersive medium** like glass or water.

questions.question: A goods train and a superfast train started running from station A and station B, respectively, at the same time towards each other on parallel tracks. If the distance between station A and station B is 154 km and trains are running at speeds of 61 km/h and 93 km/h, respectively, then at how much distance (in km) from station B will the trains meet?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both trains start at the same time, Distance ratio = Speed ratio.

Ratio of speeds (A : B) = 61 : 93.

Total distance parts = 61 + 93 = 154 units.

154 units = 154 km ⇒ 1 unit = 1 km.

Distance from Station B = 93 units = 93 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 93.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between A and B = 154 km

Speed of Goods train (from A) = 61 km/h

Speed of Superfast train (from B) = 93 km/h

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = Speed₁ + Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d3155909a397b65872611f966d9a86f674489bf55e5b4c40e408e32170c37aa.png] 

⇒ Relative Speed = 61 + 93 = 154 km/h

⇒ Time taken to meet = 154 ÷ 154 = 1 hour

⇒ Distance from Station B = Speed of train from B × Time

⇒ Distance = 93 × 1 = 93 km

**∴ The correct answer is 93.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (u + v).

Meeting Point Logic

If two objects start moving towards each other at the same time, they will meet when the sum of distances covered by both equals the total distance between them.

Constant Time Property

If the time of travel is the same for two objects, the ratio of the distances they cover is exactly equal to the ratio of their speeds (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂).

questions.question: Which chamber of the heart sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right ventricle**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human heart is a **four-chambered** muscular organ consisting of two **atria** (upper chambers) and two **ventricles** (lower chambers).
 
• The **Right ventricle** is specifically responsible for pumping **deoxygenated blood** to the lungs. It receives this blood from the right atrium and pushes it through the **pulmonary valve** into the **pulmonary artery**.
 
• The **Right atrium** receives deoxygenated blood from the entire body via the **Superior Vena Cava** and **Inferior Vena Cava**.
 
• The **Left atrium** receives **oxygenated blood** returning from the lungs through the **pulmonary veins**.
 
• The **Left ventricle** is the thickest chamber of the heart; it pumps oxygenated blood to the rest of the body through the **aorta**.
 
• The process of blood traveling from the heart to the lungs and back to the heart is known as **Pulmonary Circulation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Pulmonary Artery** is unique because it is the only artery in the human body that carries **deoxygenated blood**.
 
• Conversely, the **Pulmonary Vein** is the only vein that carries **oxygenated blood**.
 
• The **Tricuspid Valve** prevents the backflow of blood from the right ventricle into the right atrium.
 
• The **Bicuspid Valve** (also known as the **Mitral Valve**) prevents the backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium.
 
• The **Sinoatrial (SA) node**, located in the right atrium, acts as the natural **pacemaker** of the heart, initiating the electrical impulses for contraction.

The volume of a solid cylinder is 5,236 cm³ and its height is 34 cm. What is the total surface area of the solid cylinder?

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of cylinder = πr²h ⇒ 5236 = (22/7) × r² × 34

r² = (5236 × 7) / (22 × 34) = 238 × 7 / 34 = 7 × 7 ⇒ r = 7 cm

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(h + r)

TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (34 + 7) = 44 × 41 = 1804 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1804 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Height (h) = 34 cm

π = 22/7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/867788abe01784ee360ed36d0e4ae88f438d51585545533caef807f41c0d02fb.png]

⇒ Volume = πr²h

⇒ 5236 = (22/7) × r² × 34

⇒ r² = (5236 × 7) / (22 × 34)

⇒ r² = 7 × 7 = 49

⇒ r = √49 = 7 cm

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (34 + 7)

⇒ TSA = 44 × 41

⇒ TSA = 1804 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1804 cm².**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The lateral area excluding the circular bases is given by the formula: CSA = 2πrh.

questions.question: LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) is stored in cylinders in liquid form because:

options.text: It is heated and expanded under low pressure
It reacts with air to form liquid
It is cooled and compressed under high pressure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is cooled and compressed under high pressure**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas)** is a mixture of flammable hydrocarbon gases, primarily **Butane** and **Propane**.
 
• At normal atmospheric temperature and pressure, these substances exist in a gaseous state. However, to store them efficiently in cylinders for domestic and industrial use, they must be converted into a liquid form through a process called **Liquefaction**.
 
• The **Liquefaction** of gas is achieved by **increasing the pressure** and **decreasing the temperature** (cooling). **High pressure** forces the gas molecules closer together, while **cooling** reduces their kinetic energy, allowing them to condense into a liquid.
 
• Storing LPG as a liquid is highly advantageous because liquids occupy much less volume than gases. This allows for a **higher energy density**, meaning a large amount of fuel can be stored and transported in a relatively small **steel cylinder**.
 
• When the valve of the cylinder is opened, the pressure drops, and the liquid turns back into a gas (vaporizes) before reaching the burner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ethyl Mercaptan** (also known as ethanethiol) is a strong-smelling chemical added to LPG as an **odorant**. Since pure LPG is **odorless**, this additive helps in detecting gas leaks and preventing accidents.
 
• LPG is **heavier than air**; therefore, in the event of a leak, it tends to settle at ground level or in low-lying areas, which can pose a fire hazard.
 
• LPG is considered a **cleaner fuel** compared to coal or wood because it produces fewer greenhouse gases and particulates during combustion.
 
• The main components of LPG are **Propane** (C3H8) and **Butane** (C4H10).

questions.question: Which of the following hormones is secreted by the pituitary gland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth hormone**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Growth hormone** (also known as **somatotropin**) is secreted by the **anterior pituitary gland**. It is essential for human development as it stimulates **growth**, **cell reproduction**, and **cell regeneration**.
 
• **Adrenaline** (epinephrine) is produced and secreted by the **adrenal medulla**, which is part of the **adrenal glands** located on top of the kidneys. It is primarily involved in the **fight-or-flight response**.
 
• **Thyroxine** (T4) is the main hormone secreted into the bloodstream by the **thyroid gland**. It plays a vital role in regulating the body **metabolic rate**, heart and digestive functions, and muscle control.
 
• **Insulin** is a hormone produced by the **beta cells** of the **pancreatic islets** (Islets of Langerhans) in the **pancreas**. It regulates the **glucose** levels in the blood by facilitating the cellular uptake of glucose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **pituitary gland** is often called the **master gland** because its hormones control other parts of the **endocrine system**, such as the thyroid gland, adrenal glands, ovaries, and testes.
 
• It is a small, pea-sized gland located at the base of the **brain**, just below the **hypothalamus**.
 
• Other hormones secreted by the **anterior pituitary** include **Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)**, **Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)**, **Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)**, **Luteinizing hormone (LH)**, and **Prolactin (PRL)**.
 
• The **posterior pituitary** does not produce its own hormones but stores and releases two hormones produced by the **hypothalamus**: **Oxytocin** and **Antidiuretic hormone (ADH)** (also known as vasopressin).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the parts individually: 9² = 81, √(8²) = 8, √49 = 7.

Expression becomes: 81 + 8 − (10 × 7) − 20

Combine positive and negative terms: 89 − 70 − 20

89 − 90 = −1

**∴ The correct answer is -1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: 9² + √(8²) − 10√49 − 20

Method: Apply BODMAS rule (Bracket, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ Step 1 (Calculate powers and roots): 9² = 81

⇒ √(8²) = 8

⇒ √49 = 7

⇒ Step 2 (Substitute values): 81 + 8 − 10 × 7 − 20

⇒ Step 3 (Multiplication): 81 + 8 − 70 − 20

⇒ Step 4 (Addition): 89 − 70 − 20

⇒ Step 5 (Subtraction): 89 − 90

⇒ −1

**∴ The correct answer is -1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Mathematical operations must follow the priority: Brackets ( ), Orders (x², √), Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Properties of Roots

The square root of a squared number results in the absolute value: √x² = |x|. Also, √(a × b) = √a × √b.

Perfect Squares

Memorizing squares up to 30 is helpful for exams: 7²=49, 8²=64, 9²=81, 10²=100.

questions.question: A concave mirror is used in torches and car headlights because it:

options.text: Can produce a parallel beam of light

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Can produce a parallel beam of light**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror with its reflecting surface curved inwards. It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it tends to collect light that falls on it.
 
• In devices such as **torches**, **searchlights**, and **car headlights**, the light source (bulb) is placed exactly at the **principal focus** of the concave mirror.
 
• According to optical principles, any light ray passing through or originating from the **focus** of a concave mirror will emerge **parallel to the principal axis** after reflection.
 
• This specific arrangement allows the mirror to produce a **powerful, concentrated, and parallel beam of light** that can travel long distances, which is essential for visibility during night driving or searching.
 
• **Incorrect Options Analysis:**
 
 
• **Always forms virtual images:** This is incorrect. A concave mirror can form both **real** and **virtual** images depending on the distance of the object from the mirror.
 
• **Scatters light in all directions:** This is incorrect. A **convex mirror** or a rough surface scatters light, whereas a concave mirror **converges** light.
 
• **Reduces the brightness of light:** This is incorrect. By directing the rays into a beam, it actually **increases the effective brightness** in a specific direction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dentist Mirrors:** Concave mirrors are used by dentists to see a **magnified and erect image** of the teeth by placing the tooth within the focal length of the mirror.
 
• **Shaving/Makeup Mirrors:** They are used to see a **larger image** of the face for more precise grooming.
 
• **Solar Furnaces:** Large concave mirrors are used to **concentrate sunlight** at a single point to produce high temperatures for melting metals or generating power.
 
• **Sign Convention:** The **focal length** of a concave mirror is always taken as **negative** in the Cartesian sign convention.
